text:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: P1 - Hosted runtime: sudden spike in KV cache memory leading to OOM and 5xxs across a subset of routes. Paging oncall: @ben

ben: I got paged at 09:12. Already seeing elevated 5xx from hosted runtime, top traces point to kv-cache allocations blowing up for a few customer shards.

maya (eng-runtime): looking. Early hypothesis: continuous batching + aggressive prefetch for long-context requests caused KV window to grow unbounded for some sessions.

jeff: which model pool / host group?

maya: hosted-prod-eu-1, runtime v2.18. The batcher observed many long prompts (~>200k tokens across prefixes) and prefetch reached 2x normal KV entries. Memory scaled non-linearly. Logs:

```
[2026-03-15T09:10:34Z] kv_cache: insert key=shard-42 len=125000 mem=1.2GB total=78GB
[2026-03-15T09:10:35Z] kv_cache: insert key=shard-43 len=130000 mem=1.4GB total=79.4GB
[2026-03-15T09:11:02Z] runtime: OOM killing worker pid=3897
ERROR: continuous_batcher: unexpected growth > threshold
```

anita: Are we seeing perf cliffs or full cluster OOM? impact graph shows 504s for ~7% of trafic each minute between 09:10-09:22.

ben: customer impact: a few enterprise tenants reported timeouts on long-report generation. Support alerted. @support-ops please gather affected org_ids.

support-ops: collecting now. Preliminary list: org_310, org_912, org_471. Notifying account teams.

jeff: initial mitigation idea: throttle prefetch window size and disable prefetch on sessions above 4k tokens. Can we flip a runtime flag?

maya: yes. We have a platform config 'KV_PREFETCH_MAX_ENTRIES' and 'KV_PREFETCH_MAX_TOKENS'. Currently defaults are 10000 entries / 250k tokens for hosted-prod. Propose immediate hotfix: set KV_PREFETCH_MAX_TOKENS=50000 and KV_PREFETCH_MAX_ENTRIES=1000 for hosted-prod-eu-1.

ben: apply as emergency config change, then restart workers with zero-downtime rolling restart. I'll coordinate.

maya: patch command (rolling update via infra api):

```
curl -X POST https://infra-api.redwood/v1/runtime/configs/hosted-prod-eu-1/patch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $INFRA_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"KV_PREFETCH_MAX_TOKENS":"50000","KV_PREFETCH_MAX_ENTRIES":"1000"}'
```

ben: executing now. Running rolling restart with max_unavailable=1.

sre-bot: deploy-started hosted-prod-eu-1 / change KV_PREFETCH_* by ben at 09:16

maya: also enabling an emergency server-side guard to cap per-session KV memory to 256MB to avoid unbounded growth. Quick patch:

```
// runtime guard pseudo
if (session.kv_memory > 256MB) {
  stop_prefetch(session);
  mark_session_throttled();
}
```

jeff: do it. This is safer than leaving long sessions to grow.

ben: rolled patch to 10% of hosts (canary). Monitoring.

sre-bot: canary deploy success (10%) at 09:18. Metrics: 5xxs down 60% on canary hosts.

anita: thumbs up. Are we safe to roll to 100%? Any regressions on latency?

maya: latency impact minimal (+10-30ms p95). Prefetch throttling reduces memory pressure. No functional regressions observed in canary. Plan: full rollout over 15 minutes.

ben: rolling to 100% now.

sre-bot: rollout 100% complete at 09:25. 5xx rate returned to baseline by 09:28.

support-ops: notified customers at 09:30, sent incident ack and ETA for follow-up. No data loss. Some requests truncated or returned 5xx during the window.

jeff: root cause summary (first pass): continuous batching + aggressive prefetch allowed per-session KV entries to accumulate for very long prompts (rare but high-impact). Our prefetch config didn't cap token count per session tightly enough. Also missing a hard per-session kv memory cap.

maya: agreed. Immediate actions: (1) keep the hotfixed prefetch caps for hosted-prod for 48h, (2) ship permanent runtime guard (per-session kv memory cap + eviction policy) in next minor release, (3) add synthetic workload test that simulates extreme long prompts to catch this in staging, (4) alerting: add OOM spike + kv entries per-session threshold to pager.

anita: ops actions: create post-incident customer timeline, outreach plan for affected customers, coordinate billing/credits if needed.

ben: handoff to daytime oncall @maya in 2h. I'm going to sleep. Leave me the postmortem draft and timeline.

maya: taking over. Adding owner tags and will run follow-up.

jeff: small follow-up hotfix PR link: https://git.redwood/eng-runtime/pulls/3281 - implements hard per-session cap and tests.

sre-bot: incident resolved at 09:28. Severity: P1 -> resolved. Postmortem owner: maya. Action items created: PM-312 (postmortem), ENG-783 (runtime guard), QA-112 (stability tests), SRE-201 (alerting).

ben: :thumbsup: Great work.

maya: leaving notes in incident channel and will open full postmortem doc. If anyone sees regression after rollout ping me.

support-ops: closing customer notifications loop. Will update support tickets with timeline.

jeff: quick reminder - add a test scenario with a streaming client that repeatedly extends context; we missed that in perf harness.

anita: noted. Assigning to QA.

--- end thread ---
